tutorial.title: Build a basic stage
tutorial.intro: Twelve short steps from an empty room to a PDF: layers, a sketched room, a raised stage floor, portal, main curtain, batten, truss, fixtures, patch and a sheet. Each step points at the tool and moves on by itself once the drawing has what it asks for.
tutorial.done_step: Done. Next when you are ready.
tutorial.look: The outlined control is not on screen right now: check the view or the panel named in the text.
tutorial.finished.title: That's the stage.
tutorial.finished.text: Everything you clicked was a command: ⌘K finds all of them by name, and the same commands drive StageCraft from scripts or an AI. Help > Tutorial starts the tour again.
tutorial.layers.title: Layers: Stage and House
tutorial.layers.text: A layer here is a storey: a name and an elevation, nothing else. Looks and visibility by theme come from tags (Tags panel), not from classes. Keep the layer Stage and add House with +, then type its name. An elevation such as −1000 puts the stalls a metre lower; every height you type is measured from the layer.
tutorial.walls.title: Sketch the room
tutorial.walls.text: Wall tool. Click the corners; type a length in metres and Enter for an exact side, Shift keeps it square. Click the first corner to close the room. The walls follow the layer's constraint sketch: typed lengths become dimensions, double-click one later to change it and the room follows.
tutorial.floor.title: Stage floor at 1 m
tutorial.floor.text: Floor tool. First set Top height to 1000 on the options row (thickness below it), then click the corners (they snap to the room's sketch corners) and close with a click on the first corner or Enter. Top height and thickness stay editable in the Inspector.
tutorial.portal.title: Portal
tutorial.portal.text: Portal tool. One click at the centre of the opening on the setting line, y = 0. Opening and height come from the options row and stay parameters in the Inspector.
tutorial.curtain.title: Red main curtain
tutorial.curtain.text: Curtain tool. Click both ends just upstage of the portal; curtains come in theatre red. Then, with the Select tool, click it and name it Main curtain in the Inspector, where opening, fullness and gather are too.
tutorial.batten.title: A batten
tutorial.batten.text: Batten tool. Click upstage of the curtain: y is the distance from the setting line, the trim height comes from the options row. The Table's Fly bars view is the batten list with loads.
tutorial.truss.title: A truss
tutorial.truss.text: Truss tool. Click start and end, or type a length. Profile and height are on the options row; its load adds up from what hangs on it.
tutorial.fixtures.title: Fixtures from the library
tutorial.fixtures.text: In the Library, add the demo fixture types (or Import your own GDTFs). Click a type to pick it for the Fixture tool, then click on the batten or the truss to hang fixtures. Place at least two; weight and DMX footprint come from the GDTF.
tutorial.patch.title: Patch in the Table
tutorial.patch.text: Click FID 1, type 101 and Enter; Shift-click the last FID and press Fill series. Same with Address: type 1.001 in the first row, select down and Fill series patches by footprint. Mode is a cell too; conflicts turn red.
tutorial.sheet.title: A sheet with three viewports
tutorial.sheet.text: Switch to Sheets, create a sheet with + in the Sheets panel and add a Plan, a Section and a 3D viewport there. Drag them into place on the paper; view, scale and labels are in the Inspector.
tutorial.title.title: Title block
tutorial.title.text: Click the sheet in the Sheets list: with no viewport selected the Inspector shows the sheet. Fill in Project and Venue there; they are document fields, so every sheet's title block shows them.
tutorial.pdf.title: Export the PDF
tutorial.pdf.text: Export PDF in the Inspector, or File > Export PDF, writes all sheets into one file.
